title: Install and schedule Paperboy
summary: Deploy Paperboy through its product setup command, inspect readiness, and enable or disable its exact installed daily local 09:00 runner.
use_when: Deploy Paperboy through its product setup command, inspect readiness, and enable or disable its exact installed daily local 09:00 runner.
do_not_use_when: The request is to mutate source tasks, contact another recipient, certify STE compliance, or infer final inbox delivery.
outcome: Deploy Paperboy through its product setup command, inspect readiness, and enable or disable its exact installed daily local 09:00 runner.

interfaces.label: Replace the daily Conversations executable pin

effects: Installation selects product and provider files. Product setup creates empty schema-one state or opens supported existing state without copying it under ordinary admission and the runner lock. Explicit schedule enable or disable changes only paperboy/daily.

The product command retargets and selects the existing daily definition directly, preserving timer, arguments, environment, outputs and failure incidents. It preserves saved enabled intent unless enabled is explicitly supplied. Deployment creates no hold, drains no requester and temporarily disables no binding.
authority: Paperboy owns summary and occurrence success; providers retain their source, execution, activation, credential and transport authority.
success: A report exists when its summary commits; a send succeeds when acceptance is retained. Installation succeeds when product setup commands complete, without artifact-integrity, state-integrity or operational-readiness checks. Schedule enable succeeds when Clockwork commits its binding.
failure_and_recovery: Retain failed or uncertain operation state and completed deployment effects. The executor performs no automatic retry, rollback or application recovery. Resume the same brief and exact request; use a new job only for explicit retry after terminal failure. Inspect Resend before reconciling uncertain email. Preserve separately acquired maintenance holds.

The product-owned schema-two daily definition declares halt-until-approved. Nonzero report completion, start failure, crash or timeout ends the current activation. Clockwork permits later activations before the shared service-health threshold. By default, five consecutive failed read-only checks, at least 60 seconds apart, establish the halt and alert eligibility together. Healthy or inactive checks clear a pending failure episode. An established halt requires exact continuation approval; failed brief retry and uncertain-email reconciliation remain separate Paperboy operations. Binding changes and maintenance do not clear established halts.
privacy: Source text can enter private tool replies and Nucleus records; final email text leaves for Resend and the personal inbox provider. Secrets never enter prompts, product records or Clockwork definitions.
does_not_authorize: Catalog presence does not authorize an ad hoc send, enabling the schedule, changing providers, deleting private records, or treating uncertain acceptance as absence.

consumers.statement: The current user and authorized installed local Paperboy runner.

preconditions.statement: Cell deployment uses committed local main and an explicit selected product set. Select required dependency updates explicitly. Product setup uses ordinary admission and the runner lock; an existing hold can refuse it. Schedule enable requires the selected installed Paperboy executable. Installation and schedule authority are separate from discovery.

Prompt preparation requires initialized private Bazaar state and a complete cell.prompts.paperboy selection. The default database is ~/.local/share/bazaar/bazaar.sqlite3; callers accept an absolute CELL_BAZAAR_DATABASE override. Reads fail without creating state or using embedded fallback text.

inputs.statement: Brief identity or occurrence, absolute requested timeframe, source pointers, and versioned fixed agent instructions. The initial task contains no preloaded conversation content.

Deployment accepts optional enabled. Without it, absent bindings remain absent and existing disabled bindings remain disabled. A repeated executor request ID returns retained evidence and executes no instruction again; a new attempt requires a new request ID.

CONVERSATIONS_CODEX selects an absolute Codex executable for conversation reads. Schedule enable captures this selection in its environment. Supply an explicit replacement when repinning a conversation schedule; coordinated deployment preserves its selected environment. Decision report schedules do not use this executable.

--report decisions selects Annals acceptance-time reporting and requires an absolute --annals-config for an identity-bound decisions library. The default kind is conversations. Ad hoc --from and --until accept an inclusive/exclusive RFC3339 interval.

outputs.statement: JSON envelopes expose requested brief/attempt selections and acceptance receipts. Preview exposes the exact stored subject/body. Errors describe the failed operation; process success is not inbox receipt.

data_semantics.statement: A brief owns one requested interval and accepted immutable summary. An agent attempt owns one exact job request and durable tool replies. An email attempt represents one Email invocation. Source retrieval remains agent-directed.

The single paperboy/daily binding selects either conversations or decisions through retained runner arguments. Selecting decision reports replaces the daily conversation selection; ad hoc reports remain independent.

identity_and_units.statement: Brief and attempt IDs are stable UUIDs. Daily identities distinguish report kind and local 09:00 cutoff; ad hoc identities are independent. Record and filter times use Unix seconds; Annals accepted_at uses RFC3339. Windows are inclusive/exclusive and default to 86400 seconds; explicit ad hoc bounds replace that duration.

completeness_and_freshness.statement: History is read live on demand. Provider page failures remain errors. Tool pagination reports selected_count, offset, next_offset and has_more for the filtered metadata or message collection. Brief list limits only brief metadata. No snapshot, machine-wide event completeness or independent generated-text accuracy is asserted.
No maximum source age, launch delay, model start/completion time or inbox receipt time is promised.

access.statement: The typed Nucleus client and Conversations library perform agent execution and on-demand reads. Clockwork uses its provider-owned typed CLI client. Email uses its installed credential-loading CLI. Agent workspace, local execution and web access are disabled. The decision tool uses annals_api::Client::{start,watermark,read_page} against the selected config.

lifecycle_and_consistency.statement: Explicit run-owned holds block admissions, and explicit drain counts all nonterminal Paperboy jobs. The deployment command uses ordinary admission and the runner lock to initialize or open supported state after program selection. It creates and releases no hold and invokes no doctor. Completed effects remain after failure.

The product command retargets and selects the existing daily definition directly, preserving timer, arguments, environment, outputs and failure incidents. It preserves saved enabled intent unless enabled is explicitly supplied. Deployment creates no hold, drains no requester and temporarily disables no binding.

Callers resolve cell.prompts.paperboy to exact component versions before preparing new work. Prompt edits affect new selections. Retained requests, packet inputs, library revisions, and assignment snapshots preserve their existing recovery and retention semantics.

operational_limits.statement: One active product runner, 1200-second active agent timeout, 1800-second total agent wait, 2100-second Clockwork timeout, and 180-second Email invocation observation. History pages contain up to 100 records; final body is at most 64000 UTF-8 bytes. Decision pages have at most 200 events and 4 MiB of document bytes.
No throughput, future history-retention, automatic language certification, unlimited retry or unlimited deduplication guarantee.

compatibility_and_evolution.statement: Private schema 1, daily-report and decision-report toolsets: historical version 1 and new selection version plus 1. Existing conversation requests retain their meaning. No database migration is required for decision source pointers.
No general future compatibility window or deprecation period.

Selection version 1 preserves the migration baseline for historical execution. Changed tool descriptions use new immutable Nucleus toolset identities; permission policy and structural schemas remain caller-owned.

reliances.statement: Conversations supplies normalized local history and stable source identities.
Nucleus supplies constrained execution, mailbox durability and managed authentication.
Email supplies fixed personal-recipient submission and provider acceptance.

Clockwork supplies exact release activation, the shared service-health delay for halt-until-approved, retained incident notification, exact continuation approval, schedule selection and runtime history.

Cell prepares artifacts and executes explicitly ordered instructions. Paperboy owns its setup, state and schedule operations. Executor reconciliation records unknown effects and acknowledgement releases only executor admission; no application recovery is inferred.
Annals supplies unchanged accepted Krisis documents, acceptance times and feed start/watermark/page reads through its typed CLI client. Decision reports require the start operation.
Bazaar supplies immutable text versions. The caller owns selection JSON, rendering, permissions, and execution; a string supplies no additional authority.
